title: QPS scaling probe notebook (interactive)
content:
Purpose:
Quick interactive scratchpad to capture QPS scaling behavior on the current runtime build (post-quantize-optimizer merge). Focus: identify sustainable QPS for 8xA100 pool with default dynamic batching and autoscale=on, and surface non-linear latency inflection points. Notes are messy — for my own recollection.

Environment:
- Model: mosaicml/ggml-redwood-7b-v1 (fp16 / quantized 4bit fallback)
- Hardware: in-house 8xA100 dedicated pool (nvlink off for these runs)
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (post PR 842 changes), kernel selector v2
- Traffic generator: locust + small custom client for KV-cache warmup (see linked PR)
- Config snapshot used: dynamic_batch_max_tokens=2048, batching_delay_ms=6, autoscale.min=2, autoscale.max=20, kv_cache_enabled=true

Key variables I swept:
- offered_qps: 50 -> 5000 (stepwise)
- concurrency per worker: 1 -> 32
- batch size target: auto (observe), and manual overrides at 8/16/32 seekers
- request tokens: prompt length 64, response target 256 (avg 140 tokens actually)

Quick procedure:
1) Warmup: send 200 short requests (prompt 8 tokens) to populate tokenizer and initial kernels.
2) KV warmup: run 20 requests that reuse prefix to warm KV cache (important for multi-turn).
3) For each offered_qps level: spin locust for 3 minutes steady state, capture p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, batch sizes, and queued requests.
4) Follow up 2-minute cooldown between levels to let autoscaler adjust.

Raw observations (high level):
- 50-200 qps: p50 60-80ms, p95 ~180-250ms, batching mostly 1-4 tokens (very small). Utilization low (GPU 12-28%).
- 200-800 qps: p50 climbs to 90-140ms, p95 300-600ms. Batching increases (8-32 tokens per batch), GPU util 30-60%. Autoscaler increased replicas from 2->6 around 400 qps.
- 800-1800 qps: p50 ~150-300ms, p95 ~700-1500ms. Observed microbursting in queue depth every ~45s correlated with background SRE jobs (suspect noisy neighbor). Batch sizes sometimes peek to 64 when request coalescing triggers; this reduces GPU efficiency (long tail). GPU util 65-85%.
- 1800-2500 qps: latency inflection. p95 jumps non-linearly (1500ms -> 3s). GPU util saturates ~92-99%, sustained queuing. Autoscaler tries to add replicas but rollout latency ~30-45s causes transient spike windows.
- >2500 qps: system becomes unstable; p99 > 8s, request timeouts observed at 10s, backpressure kicks in from client. Manual throttle required.

Detailed notes / anomalies:
- Warmup matters a lot: cold-start p95 at 400 qps was 2x higher if KV warmup skipped. Suggest adding quick KV warmup in client library.
- Batching delay=6ms seems conservative; increasing to 12ms reduced p95 under medium load (400-800 qps) by ~18% due to larger, more efficient batches. But under very high qps this increased p50 slightly — tradeoff.
- Autoscaler ramp latency is primary cause of spikes between 800-2000 qps. Scaling steps: add 2 replicas every 30s; our workload requires smaller steps but faster reaction (add 1 replica earlier).
- I saw one steady pattern: every ~60s there is a 200-400ms p95 blip correlated with GC cycles in python-based preprocessor (worker logs show 80-120ms GC). Might rewrite critical path to avoid Python GC at high QPS.
- Large batch peaks (64+) cause KV cache thrash when requests with different prefixes get grouped; the batching heuristic needs prefix-awareness to avoid mixing unrelated chats.

Representative sample output (from locust run at 1200 qps):
- Duration: 180s
- Avg batch size: mean 22, median 20, 95th 48
- p50: 190ms, p95: 920ms, p99: 1.8s
- GPU util: 78%
- Replica count: 8
- Queued requests avg: 14

Hypotheses:
- H1: Autoscaler step size + cooldown causes transient queueing; smaller/faster steps reduce p95 spikes.
- H2: Batching heuristic that ignores prefix is harming tail latency during chatty workloads—prefix-aware batching will lower p99.
- H3: Python preprocessing GC causes periodic latency blips; move to a C extension or offloaded process to minimize pauses.

Quick experiments to run next (TODOs):
- [ ] Run identical sweep with batching_delay_ms=12 and 18; compare p50/p95/p99 curves.
- [ ] Try prefix-aware batching flag on a dev branch (simple hash of conversation id) to see p99 impact.
- [ ] Autoscale policy: change step=+1 replica and cooldown=15s; re-evaluate at 1000-2200 qps.
- [ ] Reproduce microburst with cpu/mem profiling turned on for preprocessor to confirm GC involvement.
- [ ] Long run (30m) at 1600 qps to see sustained behavior and NVLink offload effects.

Notes to self:
- Keep an eye on slow starts immediately after deploy; warmup scripts should be part of rollout.
- Communicate to SRE about noisy neighbor jobs around 10:12-10:20 PDT; check cron jobs on infra.

Quick conclusion (working):
- For this model+pool, sustainable P95 target < 1s appears feasible up to ~1400 qps with tuning (batching delay bump, autoscale tuning, prefix batching). Beyond ~1800 qps, diminishing returns and queuing make latencies unpredictable unless we increase pool capacity or reduce per-request compute (smaller model / quantization).

Links/refs: see linked_artifacts for infra PR and tracker. Also saved raw CSVs under /tmp/elliot/qps-sweeps/ (copied to artifacts later).

Timestamped log snippets:
- 2025-02-11 09:42:00 — baseline run 400 qps, p95 480ms.
- 2025-02-12 13:01:30 — warmup disabled by accident; p95 doubled at 600 qps. Re-ran.
- 2025-02-25 16:05:10 — increased batching_delay to 12ms, p95 at 800 qps fell 20%.

End of notebook — will tidy into a short memo if findings hold after next runs.
